title: Global etiology of bacterial meningitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis

claims.text: Across all age groups, S. pneumoniae and N. meningitidis are the predominant pathogens in all regions, accounting for 25.1-41.2% and 9.1-36.2% of bacterial meningitis cases respectively.
claims.byte_quote: In all age groups, *S*. *pneumoniae* and *N*. *meningitidis* were the predominant pathogens in all regions, accounting for 25.1–41.2% and 9.1–36.2% of bacterial meningitis cases, respectively.

claims.text: S. pneumoniae is the most common cause of bacterial meningitis in the 'all children' group, ranging from 22.5% (Europe) to 41.1% (Africa).
claims.byte_quote: *S*. *pneumoniae* infection was the most common cause of bacterial meningitis in the 'all children' group, ranging from 22.5% (Europe) to 41.1% (Africa)

claims.text: In all adults, S. pneumoniae frequency ranges from 9.6% (Western Pacific) to 75.2% (Africa).
claims.byte_quote: in all adults ranging from 9.6% (Western Pacific) to 75.2% (Africa)

claims.text: In neonates in Africa, E. coli and S. pneumoniae were the most common pathogens (17.7% and 20.4% respectively).
claims.byte_quote: *E*. *coli* and *S*. *pneumoniae* were the most common pathogens that caused bacterial meningitis in neonates in Africa (17.7% and 20.4%, respectively).

claims.text: N. meningitidis was the most common pathogen in children aged ~1-5 years in Europe (47.0%).
claims.byte_quote: *N*. *meningitidis* was the most common in children aged ±1–5 years in Europe (47.0%).

claims.text: Most neonatal bacterial meningitis is due to group B Streptococcus agalactiae, Escherichia coli, and Listeria monocytogenes, while most cases in children and adults are caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria meningitidis.
claims.byte_quote: Among neonates, most cases of bacterial meningitis are due to group B *Streptococcus agalactiae*, *Escherichia coli*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, while most cases in children and adults are caused by *Streptococcus pneumoniae* and *Neisseria meningitidis*.

claims.text: Haemophilus influenzae is implicated in bacterial meningitis across all age groups but is preponderant in children under 5 years of age.
claims.byte_quote: Although *Haemophilus influenzae* is implicated in bacterial meningitis in all age groups, it is preponderant in children <5 years of age.

claims.text: Weighted-mean frequency across regions/age groups ranged 3.2-47.0% for N. meningitidis and 9.6-75.2% for S. pneumoniae; H. influenzae ranged 0.2-15.5%.
claims.byte_quote: *N*. *meningitidis*, and *S*. *pneumoniae*; with weighted means for frequency across geographical regions and age groups ranging from 3.2–47.0%, and 9.6–75.2%, respectively. The range of weighted means for frequency of *H*. *influenzae* was 0.2–15.5%
